en: The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra, one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vinītadeva of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
There was a great assembly of sixty-two thousand bhikṣus, eighty billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and sixty billion and one hundred thousand upāsakas from the kingdom of Magadha.
At that time, having completed the summer retreat, the World-Honored One entered the *dharmatā-samādhi* as he approached the time of his parinirvāṇa.

Having entered this samādhi, the trichiliocosm was universally adorned: silk streamers, banners, and canopies were suspended; precious incense vases were set out; it was decorated with various perfumes, and thousand-petaled lotuses were scattered everywhere.
At that time, hundreds of thousands of millions of assemblies from this trichiliocosm, along with hundreds of thousands of millions of Brahmā kings and their retinues, came to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated with their heads at his feet, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and withdrew to stand to one side.

Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of devaputras from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, as well as kings of the Vaśavartin deities, kings of the Mahāvaśavartins, dragon kings, yakṣa kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, and mahoraga kings, each accompanied by hundreds of thousands of millions of retinues, who came to the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, they prostrated with their heads at his feet, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of great majestic virtue, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, came to the place where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, this trichiliocosm, up to its very summit, was entirely gathered together; the great assembly filled it completely, leaving no empty space between them.
At that time, there were yet others of great power—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth—who all came to assemble.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with right mindfulness manifest before him, arose from samādhi and surveyed the great assembly.
He yawned and stretched like a lion king; he did so three times.
At that time, the World-Honored One extended his broad and long tongue from the opening of his mouth, completely covering the trichiliocosm.
Having manifested this supernatural power, the Tathāgata then surveyed the great assembly.
At that time, the entire great assembly rose from their seats, joined their palms in prostration, and remained silent.
Then the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying: "Ajita!
The Tathāgata will soon enter parinirvāṇa.
If you have any doubts regarding the various dharmas, I am now present; if you wish to ask anything, this is precisely the right time.
"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, do not give rise to sorrow or regret.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One!"
You well know the proper time.
All Buddha-Tathāgatas have reached the ultimate realization of all dharmas; we pray that you will proclaim them, so that this Eye of Dharma may long abide in the world.

At that time, in the assembly, there was the Great Lord Maheśvara Devaputra, surrounded by a retinue of eight billion devas from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens. They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Dharma-gate was already proclaimed in the past by immeasurable Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will now further expound upon this for the benefit and peace of immeasurable humans and devas, so as to enable the Buddha-dharma to abide long in the world.
At that time, the World-Honored One silently gave his consent.

At that time, the Devaputra Maheśvara, knowing that the Buddha had granted his permission, leaped for joy with great exultation; he joined his palms in prostration, withdrew to one side, and stood there.
Then the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying: "Ajita!"
This Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Dharma-gate was not spoken by me alone; the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions in the past, future, and present also constantly proclaim it.

If there are sentient beings who, regarding what has been spoken by the Buddha, say it was not spoken by the Buddha, and who slander the Dharma and the Saṅgha—those slanderers shall fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya, saying:

“If there are sons or daughters of good family who resolve upon bodhicitta and receive, uphold, read, recite, and further explain to others this Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra, you should know that such persons shall not fall into the evil realms.”
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, saying: "Ajita!

From the night I attained Buddhahood until the time I am about to enter *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa*, during this interval, has there ever been any forgetfulness, lapse, or arising of evil karma regarding what my body, speech, and mind have done, said, thought, or contemplated?"
Maitreya Bodhisattva said:
"No, World-Honored One."
The Buddha said:
"Maitreya, it is as you have said."
From my attainment of enlightenment until my parinirvāṇa, everything I have said and taught during that interval is entirely true and free from falsehood.
If there are foolish people who do not understand the skillful means employed by the Tathāgata in his teachings, they will say:
"This dharma is thus; this dharma is not thus."
"Those who slander the True Dharma as well as the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others— I declare that such persons are headed for hell. The Buddha said, "Ajita!"

After my parinirvāṇa, in the world of the five turbidities, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who are not truly bodhisattvas yet claim to be bodhisattvas, they are merely followers of external paths.
Because he had previously made offerings to various Buddhas and generated the power of aspiration, he was able to leave the household life within the Buddha’s Dharma and Vinaya.

Wherever he went, he sought after many friends, fame, and gain; he acted with unrestrained impurity, abandoned his faith, and accomplished evil deeds. He failed to exercise self-restraint or self-discipline, greedily craving all manner of profit and offerings. He remained utterly remote from all Dharma-gates and from the attainment of the firm samādhi, truly possessing no knowledge whatsoever.

For the sake of their kinsmen, they falsely claim knowledge and understanding, dwelling in deceit and crookedness, speaking one thing with their mouths while acting otherwise with their bodies. "Ajita!
My path to enlightenment is entirely equal toward all sentient beings; abiding in great compassion, I employ skillful means with right mindfulness, never forgetting.
The Tathāgata abides in the power that is peerless, and teaches the Dharma without obstruction or hindrance.
If there are sentient beings who speak thus:
"The sūtras spoken by the Buddha for the śrāvakas should not be studied or heard by bodhisattvas; these are not the true Dharma, these are not the true Path;
nor should the Dharma of the pratyekabuddhas be studied."
He further spoke these words:
"The dharmas practiced by the bodhisattvas are not to be studied nor heard and received by śrāvakas;
the same applies to the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas."
Furthermore, he spoke these words:
"Whatever speech the bodhisattvas may utter, śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas should not listen to or accept it.
Their words and deeds contradict one another and do not accord with the sūtras."
"Unable to believe and accept the teaching as it truly is—the Dharma of genuine liberation—those who rely on such a teaching cannot even be reborn in heaven, let alone attain liberation. Ajita!"
I now preach the Dharma to subdue sentient beings according to their respective faiths, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. "Ajita!
I now wish to go to the worlds of the ten directions to preach the Dharma in accordance with the needs of beings, for their benefit."
It is not for those who are not truly Bodhisattvas yet put on the appearance of being Bodhisattvas, nor for those who are malicious, deceitful, or of little learning.
Regarding those within my Dharma who engage in dualistic discourse—such people of dualistic speech may say:
"This is what a Bodhisattva should study; this is what a Bodhisattva should not study."

"Those who slander the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha will, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, fall into hell, from which they shall not emerge for many hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Even if they should eventually emerge, they will be born into a poor family."

In a later time, although they shall receive the prediction of enlightenment and attain supreme perfect awakening in an age of the five turbidities, it will be just as I have today attained the Buddha-way within this world of birth and death and the five turbidities.
For these reasons, you should listen attentively and understand with faith that such is the conduct of one who follows evil friends. "Ajita!

I recall that in the past, incalculable eons ago, there appeared in the world a Buddha named Vimalajvalābhyudgatarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
At that time, the lifespan of that Buddha was eighty thousand nayutas of years, and he taught the Dharma to the assembly.
"At that time, within the Dharma of the Tathāgata King Arisen from the Immaculate Flame-Radiance, there was a bhikṣu named Pure Livelihood."
He was a great Dharma master who held fourteen hundred million sections of various sutras and six million sections of Mahayana scriptures in his memory.
His speech was pure and beautiful, and his eloquence was unimpeded; he benefited immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening them.
"At that time, when the Tathāgata King of Undefiled Flame Renown was approaching his parinirvāṇa, he addressed the bhikṣu Pure Life, saying:
'In a future age, you shall protect and uphold my true Dharma-eye.'"

“At that time, having received the Buddha’s instruction, the Venerable Life-Purifier (Śuddhājīva) protected and propagated the secret treasury of all Buddhas for ten million years after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa.
He upheld, recited, and studied this Dharma-gate of the Vaipulya Dhāraṇī, deeply understanding its meaning and intent;
and throughout the eighty thousand cities of that world, he extensively expounded it to all sentient beings according to their aspirations and inclinations.”
“At that time, there was a great city named Bhadra.
He went into that city and, for eighty billion households, preached the Dharma according to their inclinations.”

At that time, eight billion people within the city attained pure faith—one hundred million beings established themselves on the path to bodhi, while seven hundred and ninety million beings established themselves in the vehicle of the śrāvakas and were thereby tamed.
At that time, the Dharma Master Śuddhajīva was again accompanied by a community of ten thousand bhikṣus as they went forth to cultivate the practices for awakening.
At that time, there was another bhikṣu in the city of Bhadra named Dharmā.
He upheld one thousand sections of the Mahāyāna sūtras and authoritative Vaipulya scriptures and attained the four dhyānas.
He transformed all sentient beings within that city solely through the Vaipulya teachings on emptiness, yet he was unable to employ skillful means to teach according to their individual inclinations.
They shall speak thus:
"All phenomena are entirely empty and quiescent; what I have spoken is truly the Buddha's teaching.
What that bhikṣu of pure livelihood has spoken is defiled and impure; this bhikṣu is not actually one of pure livelihood, yet he claims to be so."

Why is this? Because these bhikṣus do not take the various flowers they receive to offer as worship, but instead use them for themselves; the same applies to the ointment incense and powdered incense.
The bhikṣu Ājñātakauṇḍinya is foolish and lacks wisdom; he is unable to know that I have long practiced the holy life.
Since he is young and has not long been ordained, he is arrogant, lacks faith, and is full of negligence.
"These people have no understanding; they claim that this is a bhikṣu of pure livelihood who upholds the precepts.

At that time, because Dharmā slandered those who uphold the Dharma with such an evil mind, when his body perished and his life ended, he fell into hell and underwent all manner of suffering for seventy kalpas.
After seventy kalpas had passed, he fell among the animals.
Sixty kalpas later, he encountered the Buddha Gandharvaratnaprabhāsa; within that Dharma, he gave rise to the bodhicitta, yet for ninety thousand lifetimes he was still born among the animals.
After ninety thousand lifetimes had passed, he was reborn among humans; for sixty thousand lifetimes, however, he was poor, lowly, and destitute, and was perpetually without the faculty of speech.
That Bhikṣu Śuddhājīva attained pure faith in all dharmas and preached the Dharma for others.

At a later time, he encountered sixty-three nayutas of buddhas; constantly serving as a Dharma teacher and fully possessing the five supernormal powers, he exhorted those buddhas to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
“Ajita! You should know now: was the bhikṣu of pure livelihood in the past someone else?
Do not view it otherwise; he is none other than the present Buddha Amitābha.”
Ajita! You should know now: was the bhikṣu Dharma of the past anyone else?
Do not view him as another; he is none other than my own self today.
"Because of my past folly, lack of wisdom, and slander of others, I have suffered in this manner.
By reason of these karmic causes and conditions, I have attained equal and perfect enlightenment while dwelling in an age of five turbidities."

"Therefore, Ajita! If there are bodhisattvas who make dualistic assertions regarding all dharmas, by virtue of these causes and conditions, they shall attain the path of Buddhahood in the future age of the five turbidities."
"In that buddha-field, there are various māras who constantly create obstacles and hindrances during the time of preaching the Dharma.
At that time, having heard the Buddha’s words, the great assembly all wept with grief; their tears flowed profusely as they spoke these words together:
"We pray that within the Buddha-Dharma, no dualistic teachings will be proclaimed, such as those of the bhikṣu Dharmā."
At that time, there were one hundred bodhisattvas in the assembly who rose from their seats, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and wept aloud in lamentation.
Then the World-Honored One, knowing this, intentionally asked those bodhisattvas:
"O sons of good family!
"Why do you all wail and lament in this manner?
At that time, the bodhisattvas, with one voice and in unison, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"We observe ourselves and think that we, too, must possess these various obstacles of evil karma.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these words: "So it is, so it is!"
You, too, once in the past, in the presence of the Buddha Dīpaṃkara, left the household life to practice the Way within his Dharma.
After that Buddha Dīpaṃkara had entered parinirvāṇa, there was at that time a bhikṣu named Jñānakośa, whom you all slandered back then.

From that time forward, I was unable to see the Buddha, could not give rise to the bodhicitta, and failed to attain dhāraṇīs and various samādhis; only later did I come to dwell together with you all simultaneously upon the path to enlightenment.
"You, sons of good family!

At the time of the final Buddha of this Bhadrakalpa, you shall attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti). Furthermore, after passing three asaṃkhyeya kalpas thereafter while practicing the bodhisattva path, you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Therefore, noble son!
If a bodhisattva sees another bodhisattva, he should not give rise to thoughts of 'self' and 'other,' but should regard them as a stupa and as seeing the Buddha."
Therefore, when a bodhisattva sees another bodhisattva, they must not harbor divergent thoughts or conceive of them as not being Buddhas.
To give rise to such divergent thoughts is to deceive and betray oneself; one should instead uphold this principle of not forming divergent views and remain in mutual harmony, thinking:

"If I now regard a bodhisattva who has first resolved upon enlightenment as not being like a Buddha, I am deceiving all the infinite, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddhas currently residing throughout the ten directions."
"Therefore, good son!
That bodhisattvas in the future, amidst the world of the five turbidities, shall attain dhāraṇīs and samādhis—all of this is due to the majestic power of the Buddha."
Therefore, good son!
If there are those who slander such a Dharma teacher, they are slandering the Buddha; it is exactly the same, without any difference. Good son!

After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if there is a Dharma master who skillfully accords with the inclinations and desires of others to preach the Dharma for them, such that he can cause Bodhisattvas who study the Mahāyāna and the great assembly to give rise to even a single hair’s breadth of a joyful heart or to shed even a single drop of tears for a moment, you should know that all of this is the Buddha’s divine power.
"If there is a foolish person who, though not actually a bodhisattva, falsely claims to be one, slanders true bodhisattvas and the dharmas they practice, and further says:
'What does he know?'"
"What did he understand? "Maitreya!

I recall that in the past, while training as a bodhisattva in Jambudvīpa, because I cherished and honored the Dharma, I abandoned my beloved head, eyes, wife, children, and even my royal throne for the sake of a single phrase or a single verse."
Why is this? It is because they seek only the Dharma [in name].

Like those foolish people who are solely intent on fame and addicted to gain and offerings, they rely on their own meager abilities and do not go to where the Tathāgata’s Dharma-transmitters reside to listen to and receive the True Dharma.
“Maitreya! If there is mutual harmony between them, they will be able to uphold and propagate my Dharma; if there is mutual conflict and contention, the True Dharma will not prevail. Ajita!”
"You should observe this person who slanders the Dharma; having accomplished such extremely grave karmic offenses, they will fall into the three evil realms from which it is difficult to escape.
Furthermore, Maitreya!"
When I first attained Buddhahood, I extensively proclaimed the True Dharma for the sake of sentient beings through my wondrous wisdom.

If there are foolish people who do not believe or accept what the Buddha has taught—just as that bhikṣu Dharmaruci, despite having recited a thousand sections of the Mahāyāna, explained it to others, and attained the four dhyānas—because he slandered others, he suffered great torment for seventy kalpas.
How much more so for those foolish and inferior people who, possessing no real knowledge at all, speak thus:
"I am a Dharma teacher; I clearly understand the Mahāyāna and am able to propagate it widely."
They slander the Dharma-preacher who expounds the True Dharma, claiming he understands nothing; they likewise slander the Buddha-Dharma while being full of self-conceit.
If such a foolish person slanders even a single four-line verse of the Buddha’s Mahāyāna, you should know that this karma will certainly lead them to fall into hell.
Why is this? Because they slander the Buddha-dharma and its teachers.
Due to these causes and conditions, they shall constantly dwell in the evil realms and never again behold a Buddha.

Because they have previously slandered the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, they are also able to create obstacles for those who have first resolved to attain bodhicitta, causing them to retreat from the right path.
You should know that such a person adorns themselves with great karmic offenses; for immeasurable kalpas, their body will fall into hell to undergo the retribution of great suffering.
Because they looked upon those who have resolved to attain bodhicitta with evil eyes, they shall receive the retribution of being sightless.
Because they slandered those who have resolved to attain bodhicitta with harsh speech, they receive the retribution of being tongueless. "Ajita!
I do not see any other evil dharma that can surpass the gravity of the sin of destroying and disparaging one who has resolved to attain bodhicitta."
"Because of such a transgression, one falls into the evil realms; how much more so for one who slanders other bodhisattvas?

If there is a bodhisattva who, for the sake of all sentient beings, can speak according to reality, giving rise neither to the views of annihilation nor eternalism, and not asserting that sentient beings definitely exist or definitely do not exist, nor persistently clinging to the existence or non-existence of phenomena."
Ajita! A bodhisattva who trains should abide in this way.
Abiding in this way constitutes the pure and wholesome karma of all bodhisattvas; whatever they cultivate and accumulate, they do not grasp or cling to.
If there are sentient beings who give rise to attachment, you should know that such persons are born in an age of the five turbidities.
Furthermore, there are bodhisattvas who skillfully accord with the faculties and desires [of beings], able to preach the Dharma to sentient beings in various ways.
Ajita! It is by thus fully practicing the six pāramitās that a bodhisattva is able to achieve unsurpassed bodhi.
"Those foolish people, trusting in their own self-attachments, speak in this way:"
"To say, 'A bodhisattva should study only the *prajñāpāramitā* and not study the other *pāramitās*,
because the *prajñāpāramitā* is the most preeminent,' is incorrect."
Why is this? Ajita!
In the past, when King Kāśika was training as a bodhisattva, he gave up his beloved body, head, eyes, marrow, and brain.
"At that time, did this king not possess wisdom?
Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying,
"World-Honored One!"
"It is exactly as the Holy One has said; there truly is wisdom.
The Buddha told Ajita:
"Since the distant past, throughout immeasurable time, I have fully practiced the six pāramitās."
"If one does not fully cultivate the six pāramitās, one will ultimately never attain unexcelled bodhi.
"So it is, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Ajita:
"It is as you have said.

In the past, I practiced the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom for sixty kalpas each."
"That foolish person makes this false claim: 'One attains bodhi by practicing only the single perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)'—this is impossible."
Holding such views of emptiness, he intentionally delivers this impure teaching.
One who makes such a statement acts in contradiction to the Dharma through the actions of body, speech, and mind.
Although they understand the dharma of emptiness and proclaim it to others, they do not practice in accordance with that teaching regarding the dharma of emptiness.

Because they lack such practice, they remain far removed from the meaning of emptiness; harboring jealousy in their hearts, they are deeply attached to gain and profit, even more so than to their own kinsmen.
“Ajita! In the past, when I was a wheel-turning monarch, I gave away all manner of rare treasures, as well as my head, eyes, hands, and feet, yet even then I did not attain unsurpassed bodhi;

how much less so for that foolish man who, for the sake of food and drink, frequents the homes of others and proclaims only the teaching of emptiness, claiming that what he says is the path to bodhi and the practice of a bodhisattva?”
"Is this alone the true Dharma, while all other dharmas are false?
He further said:
"That which I have understood is fully testified to by immeasurable Dharma masters."
“Seeking fame and renown, they praise their own abilities and harbor malice toward those with clear understanding. Ajita!

I see that such people seek gain and offerings to sustain their lives; even if they possess virtuous conduct for a hundred kalpas, they will not attain even a small degree of the mind of dharma-patience (dharmakṣānti), let alone be able to achieve unsurpassed bodhi.”

“Ajita! I do not preach bodhi for those who deceive by having their hearts and mouths at odds; I do not preach bodhi for those who are envious; I do not preach bodhi for those who are arrogant and disrespectful; I do not preach bodhi for those who lack faith; I do not preach bodhi for those who are undisciplined; I do not preach bodhi for those who engage in sexual misconduct; I do not preach bodhi for those who judge themselves right and others wrong.”
“Ajita! Because of their arrogance, those foolish people claim to surpass the Buddha and slander the Mahāyāna sūtras spoken by the Buddha, saying they were taught by the śrāvakas of the Hīnayāna.”
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Subhūti:
“One should not teach the Prajñāpāramitā to those who hold dualistic views.
Subhūti said to the Buddha:
"So be it, World-Honored One!
It is as the Buddha has taught.
The Buddha said:
“In this way, Subhūti,
giving with a mind free from attachment is called bodhi. Subhūti said:
"So be it, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said: "Subhūti!
“Giving without praising oneself or disparaging others is called bodhi.
Subhūti said, “So it is,
World-Honored One!”
The Buddha said:

"Subhūti! Observe how foolish people give rise to the view of 'I' and 'mine,' lacking shame and remorse; for the sake of their kinsmen, out of greed for sustaining their lives, they delight in receiving the gifts of others."
"You should know that such a person is solely engaged in the creation of evil karma. Furthermore, Ajita!
A bodhisattva should not give rise to fear regarding any dharma, nor regarding any bodhisattva-dharma; regarding even one..."
Do not be terrified by any Pratyekabuddha-dharma; do not be terrified by any Śrāvaka-dharma;
do not be terrified by any dharma of ordinary worldlings; do not be terrified by any dharma of affliction;
do not be terrified by any dharma of exhaustion; and do not be terrified by difficult diligence.
Do not be afraid; thus, do not be afraid of what is or what is not, do not be afraid of what is done or what is not done,
do not be afraid of what is feared or what is not feared, do not be afraid of existence or non-existence, do not be afraid of mind or non-mind,
do not be afraid of awakening or non-awakening, and do not be afraid of karma or non-karma.
Do not be afraid; do not be afraid of the wholesome or the unwholesome, do not be afraid of the secure or the insecure,
do not be afraid of liberation or non-liberation, do not be afraid of cultivation or non-cultivation,
do not be afraid of the Dharma or non-Dharma, and do not be afraid of stillness or distraction.
Do not be terrified by the conventional or the real; do not be terrified by faith or lack of faith;
do not be terrified by wholesome thoughts or unwholesome thoughts; do not be terrified by abiding or non-abiding.
In this way, a bodhisattva should not give rise to fear regarding any phenomena. Ajita!

Because I cultivated such fearless dharmas in the past, I attained perfect enlightenment; I am able to fully comprehend the mental realms of all sentient beings, yet I do not give rise to the conceptual mark of "knowing" regarding that which is known.

I shall expound according to the capacities of beings based on what I have realized, enabling all bodhisattvas who hear this Dharma to attain the seal of the *dhāraṇī* of radiance; by attaining this seal of the Dharma, they shall never again fall back.
If one does not understand this Dharma as it truly is, lacking skillful means, one will ultimately fail to attain unsurpassed bodhi.

"Ajita! When I preach this Dharma for the sake of the sentient beings of the four continents, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, those sentient beings each see Śākyamuni Tathāgata preaching the Dharma for them."
In this manner, proceeding in succession up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, those sentient beings there also think, "The Tathāgata speaks for me alone.
Just as it is in one four-continent world system, so it is throughout the trichiliocosm; all these sentient beings harbor this thought:
"Śākyamuni Tathāgata was born solely in my own land, and he turns the great wheel of Dharma for me alone."

“Ānanda! By such great power of skillful means, I am able, throughout immeasurable and boundless worlds, to constantly survey at dawn all sentient beings who are ready to be transformed and preach the Dharma for them;
at noon and in the evening, I always observe sentient beings with the eye of Dharma and preach all dharmas for those sentient beings in those worlds.”
"In this way, all sentient beings who study as bodhisattvas should cultivate themselves within the immeasurable realms of the Buddhas.
If those foolish people slander and revile the True Dharma spoken by the Buddha, they will perversely cling to their own interpretations, taking them to be the ultimate truth."
If one slanders the Dharma, they will not believe in the Buddha; by this evil karma, they shall fall into hell and undergo all manner of suffering, never again hearing the Dharma.
"Furthermore, Ajita!
"You should receive and uphold this secret teaching of the Tathāgata, and explain it extensively for others through skillful means.
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Samantaguṇaprabha,
the Bodhisattva Niḥsaṃśaya, the Bodhisattva Cittotpādaniyata, the Bodhisattva Sūkṣmacittavikāsamanas, and the Bodhisattva Prabhāsa...
Sākyamuni, the Bodhisattva King of Joy, the Bodhisattva Fearless, the Bodhisattva Whose Mind Reaches Everywhere to Boundless Buddha-fields,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Fragrant Elephant, the Bodhisattva Who Extinguishes All Evil Karma, the Bodhisattva Abiding in Samādhi,
the Bodhisattva Adorned with Hundreds of Thousands of Merits, and the Bodhisattva Wondrous Sound from Afar.
They heard of the Bodhisattvas: the Bodhisattva Sarvajñāsmṛti, the Bodhisattva Mahānāmadūravyāhāraratnaketu-vyūha,
the Bodhisattva Sarvadharmaparyeṣaka, the Bodhisattva Buddhapadavihārin, the Bodhisattva Candraprabhavyūha,
and the Bodhisattva Sarvalokamahāparṣadvyūha— these and other such Bodhisattvas.
The Mahāsattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
It is so, it is so!"
"It is exactly as the Holy One has said.
We, from this eastern direction, having passed through Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of sixty Ganges Rivers, have paid respectful homage at the abodes of various Buddhas.
In each and every Buddha-field, we saw only Śākyamuni Tathāgata appearing in the world."
During those seven days, we traveled throughout the ten directions and saw only Śākyamuni Tathāgata appearing in the world; we beheld no other Buddhas.
Having completed our journey, we returned to our own lands to hear and receive the True Dharma.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the youth Mañjuśrī:
"You should now contemplate with careful attention that the wisdom of the Tathāgata is inconceivable, and the realm of the Tathāgata is likewise inconceivable."
Such is the Dharma of the Tathāgata—the peerless equality—and yet those foolish people speak thus:
"Only the single *prajñāpāramitā* is the practice of the Tathāgata, the practice of the Bodhisattva, and the practice of the Deathless."
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
“One who speaks thus contradicts the Dharma. Why is this?
The bodhisattva’s practice of the Dharma is exceedingly difficult to fulfill.

Practice free from attachment is the bodhisattva’s practice; practice of non-self and non-mine is the bodhisattva’s practice; practice of emptiness is the bodhisattva’s practice; practice of signlessness is the bodhisattva’s practice.
“Mañjuśrī! Such practices as these are the bodhisattva practices; those who study the bodhisattva path should uphold them in this way.
If there are foolish people who harbor wrong views, you should know that such persons do not understand my Dharma.”

“Mañjuśrī! You bodhisattvas should guard your body and speech, ensuring that you do not become negligent regarding unwholesome dharmas. Make your minds firm so as not to regress, preach the Dharma fully for the sake of all sentient beings, and you yourselves should likewise abide within the Dharma.”

"I have fully accomplished unsurpassed bodhi since incalculable kalpas ago; through skillful means, I have extensively taught it for the sake of others, enabling all sentient beings to distance themselves from the evil realms."
“Mañjuśrī! If there are foolish people who slander the subtle and wondrous Dharma, they are slandering the Buddha and are also said to be slandering the Saṃgha.
Furthermore, they speak as follows:”
"To say, 'This teaching is correct and that teaching is incorrect,' is also called slandering the Dharma. To say,
'This teaching was spoken for Bodhisattvas, and this teaching was spoken for Śrāvakas'— "
"One who speaks thus is also said to slander the Dharma.
To say, 'This is the training of a bodhisattva; this is not the training of a bodhisattva,' one who speaks thus is also said to slander the Dharma."
He further spoke these words:
"The Buddhas of the past have already passed away; the Buddhas of the future have not yet arrived; the Buddhas of the present do not abide. I alone have attained the dharma of dhāraṇī."
To speak in this manner is also called slandering the Dharma. Because one slanders the Dharma, they claim that those who have attained dhāraṇī possess impure teachings.

They revile and slander the practices cultivated by true Dharma masters; furthermore, they slander Dharma masters, saying their understanding and wisdom do not accord with their words; they further slander Dharma masters, saying their conduct deviates from the Path; they further slander Dharma masters, saying their bodies do not maintain the precepts; they further slander Dharma masters, saying their minds lack wisdom; they further slander Dharma masters, saying their intentions lack clear comprehension; they further slander Dharma masters, saying their speech lacks eloquence and clarity; and they further harbor no faith or acceptance toward the words spoken by the Tathāgata, even going so far as to say:
"This sūtra is authentic; this sūtra is not.
This verse-sūtra is authentic; this verse-sūtra is not.
This dharma is trustworthy; this dharma is not trustworthy."
When one encounters those who speak correctly, they falsely formulate divergent arguments and create obstacles for those listening to the true Dharma, claiming:
"This is practice; this is not practice";
"This is accomplishment; this is not accomplishment."
"This is the proper time; this is not the proper time.
All such statements as these are called slandering the Dharma.
"Furthermore, Mañjuśrī!"

Whether it be a śrāvaka preaching the Dharma or a bodhisattva preaching the Dharma, one should know that in all such cases it is due to the power of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual authority and protective mindfulness that causes these bodhisattvas and others to speak in this manner.

“Mañjuśrī! If such foolish people as these still give rise to slander even while the Buddha is present in the world, how much more so will those Dharma masters who receive and uphold my Dharma after my parinirvāṇa not be slandered?
Why is this? Because they belong to the retinue of Māra.
You should know that such persons fall into the evil realms.

"Just as those foolish people greedily seek gain and offerings to sustain their kin and relatives, they harbor no faith or conviction in the Tathāgata’s Dharma, and furthermore, they destroy the Tathāgata’s teachings."
Those relatives, out of a partisan spirit, went to the houses of brahmins and householders and spoke thus in praise of that foolish man:
"He is able to know and understand both the Dharma and its meaning; he is clear-sighted regarding the faculties and desires, and is skilled at preaching for others."
"Having received the faithful offerings of others without ever feeling shame or remorse, because they slandered the Dharma, both they and their retinues fell together into hell. Mañjuśrī!..."

I will never preach the bodhisattva practices to those who lack faith; nor will I preach the pure Dharma to those who are greedily attached to the household life; nor will I preach the Dharma of liberation to those with dualistic views; nor will I preach the Dharma for escaping suffering to those with one-sided views; nor will I preach the truly pure Dharma to those who delight in the world.
“Mañjuśrī! Of dharmas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I have expounded them for others with a mind free from attachment;
yet of dharmas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I have taught them to sentient beings with a mind possessed of attachment.”
"If there are sentient beings who delight in emptiness, I preach the Dharma of emptiness for them;
if there are sentient beings who delight in wisdom, I preach the Dharma of wisdom for them;
if there are sentient beings who delight in signlessness, I preach the Dharma of signlessness for them."
If there are sentient beings who delight in signs, he teaches them the Dharma of signs;
if there are sentient beings who delight in loving-kindness, he teaches them the Dharma of loving-kindness;
if there are sentient beings who delight in causes and conditions, he teaches them the Dharma of causes and conditions.
If there are sentient beings who delight in causelessness, one preaches the Dharma of causelessness:
"This is the dharma of proper deportment; this is the dharma of improper deportment;
this is the dharma of emptiness; this is the dharma of existence."
"This is a conditioned dharma; this is an unconditioned dharma;
this is a dharma of grasping; this is a dharma of obscuration;
this is a dharma of ordinary persons; this is a dharma of noble ones."
"This is a material phenomenon (rūpadharma); this is an unwholesome phenomenon;
this is the dharma of fools; this is the dharma of concentration.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Mañjuśrī.

"All such dharmas as these constitute the path of the *prajñāpāramitā*; yet those foolish people speak according to their own words, not relying on the Tathāgata’s true and pure teaching, and thus slander the Buddha’s True Dharma."
At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As the Buddha has said, such foolish people, by associating with evil friends, give rise to slander in their present lives.”
"So it is, World-Honored One!
By what causes and conditions can one avoid this fault?
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:

"In the past, for seven years, during the six periods of day and night, I repented of the grave offenses committed through the actions of my body, speech, and mind; from that time onward, I attained purity."
After ten kalpas had passed, he attained the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*). "Mañjuśrī!
You should know that this sutra is the vehicle of the bodhisattvas; it enables those who have not yet awakened to attain awakening."
If, upon hearing this sutra being preached, one does not believe or accept it, they will fall into the evil realms due to the cause of such slander.
These bodhisattvas clearly receive my Dharma, and only thereafter may they proclaim it for others; by upholding it in this manner, they can remain far removed from the evil destinies.
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
“There are four dharmas of equality that a bodhisattva should study. What are the four?
First, the bodhisattva is equal toward all sentient beings; second, equal toward all phenomena; third, equal toward awakening; and fourth, equal toward the teaching of the Dharma.
These are the four dharmas.
"A bodhisattva should know these four kinds of dharmas;
having known them, the bodhisattva explains them for the sake of sentient beings."
If there are those with faith, they will remain far removed from the evil destinies;
if there are those without faith, they shall fall into the woeful paths.
If good sons or good daughters abide in these four dharmas, you should know that such persons shall not fall into the evil destinies.
“Furthermore, there are four dharmas. What are these four?

First, to have no regressive thought toward any sentient being; second, not to disparage or revile any Dharma-preachers; third, not to give rise to slander toward those with wisdom; and fourth, to always maintain respect for everything spoken by all Tathāgatas.”
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family is able to skillfully practice and study these four dharmas, they will never fall into the various evil realms.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī!

A bodhisattva, with the seven treasures filling as many Buddha-fields as there are sands in the Ganges River, makes offerings daily for as many kalpas as there are sands in the Ganges River to as many Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as there are sands in the Ganges River.

If there are good sons or good daughters who are able to read and recite even a single sentence or a single verse of such a profound and subtle Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtra three times, the merit they obtain surpasses the merit obtained from the aforementioned acts of giving;
if there are those who recite and uphold this sūtra, the merit they obtain is many times greater than that.

Furthermore, even if there were someone who practiced the six pāramitās—generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom—the merit they obtained could not equal it.
“Mañjuśrī! This sūtra is so vast in name and meaning that it has no equal.
You bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should skillfully train in it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and extensively analyze and explain it for the sake of sentient beings.”
At that time, the entire great assembly, including all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had come from the ten directions, addressed the Buddha together, saying:
“World-Honored One! It is so, it is so!”
“As the Buddha has taught, we shall uphold it.

When this Dharma was spoken, bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of thirty Ganges Rivers attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), and bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of seventy Ganges Rivers attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

Furthermore, there were sixty-three billion hundred-thousand nayutas of great assemblies from all the trichiliocosm worlds who, upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, felt joy in their hearts and crossed the stream of birth and death for eighty kalpas;
they further became non-retrogressive regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and after sixty-three kalpas had passed, they fully accomplished unsurpassed enlightenment.

Those bodhisattvas and the entire great assembly—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they paid homage and practiced accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Vaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra
